fixed_frame.law: Uniform finite frame at Gamma=1; Gamma sensitivity reweights observed conditional law only while n/N and each missing 1/N remain fixed.

assumptions: Keep each original scenario/model fit, cohort, observed residual and group fold fixed.
Unknown event indicators may be independently 0 or 1; this mathematical extension does not claim a defined predictor or physical completion on missing rows.
Within observed rows q_i=w_i/n, sum q_i=1, w_i in [1/Gamma,Gamma], 1<=Gamma<infinity.
No measured selection propensity or exchangeability law is asserted.
finite_missing_event_theorem.proof: Event and complement density bounds intersect. For 0<e<1 choose constant within-class weights z/e and (1-z)/(1-e), attaining every z in [L,U]. At e=0 or1 z is fixed. Missing event sum attains integers 0,...,M. Add fixed block masses; endpoints are attained at z=L,k=0 and z=U,k=M. The finite set may have gaps, so report its hull rather than claiming every interior proportion attainable.
boundary_caveats: Gamma->infinity yields [0,1] only for interior observed event fraction. For e=0 the hull is [0,M/N]; for e=1 it is [n/N,1].
One common residual imposes monotone events across ordered thresholds; do not multiply pointwise bounds as independent information.
The 354/628 event-missing fraction is not physical unknown mass; physical unknown mass remains 1.
finite_missing_event_theorem.unbounded_mean_corollary: With unrestricted missing signed residual value R, the finite-frame residual mean includes (M/N)*R and is unbounded as R tends to either infinity. This is not a theorem about physical x_C or physically feasible completions.
